items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He was like a mentor to me, Paul Robinson.

ctx.x: Yeah, at that time. I pick up an Albert system clarinet and I say, “If this is what it’s about, I’m going to take up plumbing.” [laughs] “Okay. Take this thing away.” This guy Paul Robinson, he was a pretty fair saxophonist. He played tenor, but he was an excellent clarinetist. He would wipe you away on the clarinet. He took me under his wing. He played with -- I can’t remember if it was Tommy Smith’s band or Andrew Johnson’s band. He was a neighbor of mine. He didn’t live too far away. He really helped me a lot,…
Were there any competing interests for you besides music? You seem like you’ve latched on to this fairly early, had all these experiences. What else was competing for space in your head?
